courses.title: Courses Offered
courses.subtitle: Combining building physics theory with data science practice to cultivate interdisciplinary net-zero building professionals.
courses.c1_title: Introduction to Net Zero Buildings and Simulation Practice
courses.c1_overview_desc: One of the main sources of global energy consumption is the building sector. To pursue the global net-zero emission goal, this course discusses the net-zero concept for buildings and incorporates real-world case studies for practical exercises. The course systematically deconstructs building physical environments and electromechanical systems, equipping students with core capabilities to analyze causes of building energy consumption. Using EnergyPlus for quantitative analysis.
courses.c1_obj_1: Build Core Knowledge: Master building physics (heat, light, air) and systems (HVAC, lighting).
courses.c1_obj_2: Master Simulation Tools: Proficient in EnergyPlus, geometry modeling, and parameter setting.
courses.c1_obj_3: Execute Field Survey: Field measurements of NTU campus buildings.
courses.c1_obj_4: Data Analysis & Calibration: Compare simulation with meter data and calibrate parameters.
courses.phase_1: Phase 1: Building Physics & Net Zero Basics
courses.prereq_desc: Basic data analysis skills (Excel or Python) recommended.
courses.c2_title: Data Science for Environment and Energy
courses.c2_overview_desc: Data-driven decision making plays a key role in environmental sustainability. This course aims to build students' data science foundation and explore applications in environmental monitoring and energy systems. Systematically teaching Python using Colaboratory, analyzing real-world campus data (smart meters, CO2, temperature).
courses.c2_obj_1: Master Data Processing: Python for cleaning and transformation.
courses.c2_obj_2: Master Analysis & Visualization: Pandas & Matplotlib/Seaborn for EDA.
courses.c2_obj_3: Build Prediction Models: Regression/Clustering for energy consumption.
courses.c2_obj_4: Solve Real Problems: Apply to campus cases.

join.section_desc: BIEG Data Lab is actively looking for partners passionate about smart buildings, energy data science, and sustainable development. We welcome Master's students, Ph.D. students, postdocs, and research assistants with the following backgrounds to join us.
join.contact_msg: If you are interested in our research directions, please send your CV and transcript to the email below.

research.hero_desc: We focus on building energy simulation, digital twins, and grid resilience forecasting. Solving energy challenges from single buildings to urban grid scales through data-driven methods.
research.p1_desc1: This project uses the National Taiwan University campus as a testbed, integrating AMI smart meter data from over 200 buildings to establish a campus-scale 'Urban Building Energy Digital Twin'.
research.p1_desc2: Unlike traditional single-building simulations, we adopt a 'Bottom-up' modeling strategy, combining automated GIS processing and physics-driven models to develop a scalable automation framework. This platform allows users (faculty, students, managers) to visualize building energy flows and provides scientific energy-saving recommendations for retrofitting old buildings.
research.p1_t1_desc: Developing Python automation scripts to convert 2D GIS Shapefiles and DTM into 3D building geometries.
research.p1_t1_bi1: Automated extraction of floor heights and window-to-wall ratios
research.p1_t2_desc: Establishing a localized building parameter database (Archetypes) for Taiwan's climate and building codes, replacing US defaults.
research.p1_t2_bi1: Defining thermal conductivity for common RC structures in Taiwan
research.p1_t2_bi3: Integrating TMY3 typical meteorological years for Taiwan
research.p1_t3_desc: Using AMI measurements as Ground Truth and applying AI algorithms to automatically inverse unknown physical parameters.
research.p1_t3_bi2: Reducing simulation error to ASHRAE standards
research.p1_t4_desc: Conducting large-scale energy-saving 'What-if Scenario' simulations based on the calibrated digital twin model.
research.p1_t4_bi1: Evaluating benefits of replacing old windows and HVAC
research.p1_t4_bi3: Generating ROI analysis for energy-saving investments
research.p1_y1_goal: Goal: Establish campus-wide building geometry library
research.p1_y1_bi1: Integrating GIS data and Maintenance Division data.
research.p1_y2_goal: Goal: Reducing simulation vs. measurement error
research.p1_y2_bi2: Refining calibration for major energy-consuming buildings.
research.p2_desc1: Existing energy forecasting models face three main gaps: 'insufficient generalization', 'scale discontinuity', and 'lack of risk quantification'. Traditional models often fail when facing new developments or extreme weather, and cannot effectively link single-building stochasticity with regional grid smoothness.
research.p2_desc2: This project proposes an integrated AI framework combining 'Time-Series Foundation Models' and 'Hierarchical Reconciliation' to solve cross-scale energy forecasting challenges, and using 'Conformal Prediction' to provide risk intervals with statistical guarantees, enhancing grid dispatch resilience.
research.p2_t1_desc: Introducing large-scale pre-trained models like Chronos or TimesFM to solve 'insufficient generalization'.
research.p2_t1_bi2: Effectively handling 'new construction' prediction without history
research.p2_t1_bi3: Resisting data distribution shifts caused by extreme weather
research.p2_t2_desc: Using MinT (Minimum Trace) algorithm to solve the 'scale discontinuity' from single building to grid.
research.p2_t2_bi1: Ensuring sum consistency between bottom (building) and top (substation)
research.p2_t2_bi2: Optimizing prediction accuracy using matrix operations
research.p2_t3_desc: Addressing 'lack of risk quantification' by providing prediction intervals with strict statistical guarantees.
research.p2_t3_bi3: Assisting precise decision-making for grid operating reserves
research.p2_t4_desc: Building an End-to-End energy management system integrating forecasting, calibration, and optimization.
research.p2_t4_bi1: Linking 500kW building-level to GW grid-level data
research.p2_y1_bi1: Developing anomaly detection Pipeline, completing data cleaning.
research.p2_y1_bi3: Producing baseline performance report and preliminary datasets.
research.p2_y2_bi1: Introducing Chronos for Zero-shot and fine-tuning experiments.
research.p2_y2_bi2: Developing Conformal Prediction (UQ) module and validating effectiveness.
research.p2_y2_bi3: Solving high-stochasticity prediction for single buildings.
research.p2_y3_goal: Focus: MinT coordination & Open source release
research.p2_y3_bi1: Implementing MinT hierarchical coordination to bridge scale gaps.
research.p2_y3_bi3: Releasing open source datasets and technical reports.
